under:
Appellant/Accused Raja @ Drigpal Gosh in Conviction Sentence Section Act Imprisonment Fine if Imprisonment deposited in lieu of fine 363/34 IPC R.I. for five Rs.3,000/- R.I. for 02 years months 366/34 IPC R.I. for seven Rs.5,000 R.I for 02 years months Appellant/Accused Lokendra Singh Ghosh in Conviction Sentence Section Act Imprisonment Fine if Imprisonment deposited in lieu of fine 363/34 IPC R.I. for five Rs.3,000/- R.I. for 02 years months 366/34 IPC R.I. for seven Rs.5,000 R.I for 02 years months 3 CRA-3045-2023 376(1) IPC RI for ten years Rs.10,000/- R.I. for 06 months
3/4 POCSO Invoking provisions contained in Section 42 of POCSO ACT Act, conviction has been recorded under Section 376(1) of Indian Penal Code.

3. However, CRA No. 3045 of 2023 has been filed by the State Government, being aggrieved of the above mentioned impugned judgment dated 29.10.2022 for enhancement of sentence awarded to the accused persons Raja @ Drigpal Gosh and Lokendra Singh Ghosh.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that, present is a case of acquittal.

It is submitted that,
prosecutrix was admittedly a married women.

Reading from her statements recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. as contained in Ex.D-1, it is pointed out that, in her statements recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C, prosecutrix had stated that, she had called Lokendra and had informed him that she wants to live with him.
She cannot live without him and asked him to take her with him.
She stated that, Lokendra was known to her for last three years.
Lokendra had met her in the night on his motorcycle, and she had without informing anybody in her house, had come on door on her own volition.
Then, both of them had travelled to Mumbai in a train, where they stayed together in a room for 10-12 days.
Then, they returned back to Chandera where report was lodged by her parents.
5. Thus, it is submitted that, merely positivity of DNA (Ex.P-26) is not sufficient, because a relationship between two consensual adults will not be a case for conviction.
6. Shri Ajay Shukla, learned Government Advocate in his turn supports the impugned judgement and submits that, State has also filed its 4 CRA-3045-2023 appeal bearing CRA No. 3045 of 2023.
It is seeking enhancement of sentence for both the accused persons.

It is submitted that, as per record,
age of the victim was minor.

This fact has been rightly appreciated by the learned trial Court,
therefore, no indulgence is called for.

7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the records, prosecutrix (PW-1)
stated that, she belongs to Ahirwar Community, accused is of Ghoshi Community.
In her cross-examination, she admits that, at the time of the incident, she was already married.
Her marriage was performed on 22.06.2018.
She states that, the age of her husband is 20 years, he was major at the time of her marriage.
She admits that her age and the age of her husband is equal.
Then she stated that, her age is 17 years and the age of her husband is 20-21 years.

She contradicted her statements, recorded under Section 164 CR.P.C. (Ex.D-1) and stated that, Lokendra had forcefully The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Lokendra Singh Ghose on 29 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156574497/
2 established physical relationship with her, but this fact is not mentioned in her statements recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. (Ex.D-1).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She denied that, she had informed police in her statements (Ex.D- 2) that she was talking to Lokendra over phone and had gone with Lokendra to Mumbai.
She admits that, she was working as a laborer alongwith Lokendra at Mumbai.
She admits that, several other laborers were working with them, but she had never informed anybody that, Lokendra had forcefully abducted her or was threatening her.
8. In Para-8 of her cross-examination this witness (PW-1) states that, at the time of the incident, her age was 19 years.
She states that, she is eight years elder to her youngest sister.
She is four years elder to her brother.
She 5 CRA-3045-2023 admits that, marriage of a girl is performed, when she attains the age of 18 years.

In Para-10 of her cross-examination, she admits that, she had never informed either in her statements recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. (Ex. D- 1) or case diary statements (Ex.D-2) that, Drigpal had accompanied Lokendra.

9. Mother of the prosecutrix (PW-2) after having said that the age of the prosecutrix was 16 years,
she admits in her cross-examination that at the time of marriage, prosecutrix was major and therefore, her marriage was performed.
This witness further admits that, she is illiterate and puts her thumb impression.
She admits that, she does not know the date of birth of any of her children.
She admits that, marriage was performed only when she had completed 18 years of age.
She stated that, the age of her youngest child is 10 years.
She states that, her marriage was performed at the age of 16 years and about 20 years have lapsed since her marriage.
She admits that, prosecutrix was born after 01-01 years of her marriage.
10. Father of the prosecutrix (PW-3) stated that, he is illiterate.
He only puts his thumb impression.
He states that, at the time of the incident, his age was 40 years.
His marriage was performed, when he was 15 years of age.
After two years of his marriage, prosecutrix was born.
He admits that, prior to the incident, prosecutrix was already married.
He states that, police had never recorded his statements.
11. Dr. Lalita Khare (PW-6) had examined the prosecutrix.
She found that, her secondary sexual characters were well developed.
There were no injury marks on her body part, there were no injury marks on her private 6 CRA-3045-2023 parts, no definite opinion could be given in regard to violation of privacy.
This witness admits that, she had not ordered for any age determination test to determine the age of the victim, because she was not asked to do so.
12. Rekha Shukla (PW-10), Headmaster of School in which prosecutrix had studied, stated that prosecutrix had taken admission on 10.08.2007.
Her father had recorded her date of birth as 01.07.2002.

She further states that, father of the prosecutrix had signed the admission form, and therefore, she is saying that, that person was literate, but this is contrary to the evidence of the father of prosecutrix (PW-3) who states that, he is illiterate and he only knows how to put his thumb impression.

She admits that, no documentary evidence has been enclosed alongwith the admission The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Lokendra Singh Ghose on 29 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156574497/
3 form, i.e. neither it is supported with birth certificate or adhar-card or any horoscope to prove the date of birth of the prosecutrix.

entities.text: State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Lokendra Singh Ghose
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She admits that, there is an alteration in Ex.P-16, where name of the father of the prosecutrix has been cut and corrected.

13. When these facts are taken into consideration, then looking to the evidence of mother of the prosecutrix (PW-2) and father of the prosecutrix (PW-3), so also the prosecutrix (PW-1) herself,
prosecutrix was adult at the time of the incident.

Ex.P-16 does not inspire confidence, inasmuch as,
the name of the father of the prosecutrix has been cut, as is admitted by Ms. Rekha Shukla (PW-10),
Headmaster of the School.
14.
Prosecutrix has herself admitted that, Raja @ Drigpal Gosh (appellant in CRA No. 10758 of 2022) was not involved in the incident.

Therefore, as far as appellant Raja @ Drigpal Gosh is concerned, his 7 CRA-3045-2023 conviction under Section 363/34 & 366/34 of IPC is not made out,
it deserves to and is hereby set-aside.
Accordingly CRA No. 10758 of 2022 is allowed.
15. As far as appellant Lokendra Singh Ghosh in CRA No. 11147 of 2022 is concerned, it is true that,
DNA report Ex.P-26 is positive.

However, it is also true that, prosecutrix after getting marriage with somebody else, had returned back to her parental home, from where, as she has stated in her statements under Section 164 Cr.P.C. had called Lokendra and had eloped with Lokendra as she was knowing Lokendra for last 03 years.
She has also admitted that, she had not made any complaint to anybody at Mumbai where Lokendra and the prosecutrix were working with several other laborers at Mumbai.
She had not complained either about abduction or about any force or coercion.

Thus,
when evidence of the prosecutrix (PW-1), her parents (PW-2 & PW-3) so also School Teacher (PW-10) is taken into consideration, then there is no material on record to prove that prosecutrix was minor at the time of the incident.

Coupled with the fact that mother of the prosecutrix (PW-2)
has admitted that, she was major at the time of her marriage.
Admittedly, incident took place after marriage of the prosecutrix.

Therefore, prosecutrix being a consenting adult, mere positivity of DNA Report, between two consenting adults is not a circumstance to record finding of conviction under Section 376(1) of IPC or 3/4 of POCSO Act or under Section 363/34 & 366/34 of Indian Penal Code.

Consensual relationship between two adults does not call for any indulgence and therefore, on this touchstone, appeal filed by Lokendra Singh Ghosh, CRA No. 11147 of 2022 8 CRA-3045-2023 is also needs to be allowed and is hereby allowed.

His conviction recorded under Section 363/34, 366/34 &
376(1) of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act is hereby set-aside.

16. Accordingly, CRA No. 10758 of 2022 filed by the appellant Raja @ Drigpal Gosh and CRA No.
11147 of 2022 filed by the appellant Lokendra Singh Ghosh, are allowed.
17. The appellants Raja @ Drigpal Gosh and Lokendra Singh Ghosh are acquitted of all the charges.
18. Appellant Lokendra Singh Ghosh is in jail, he be released immediately, if not required in any other case.
Appellant Raja @ Drigpal Gosh is on bail.
His bail bonds are hereby discharged.
19. As far as, Criminal Appeal No. 3045 of 2023 filed by the State Government is concerned, State has failed to prove that, prosecutrix was minor at the time of the incident.

They have failed to rebut The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Lokendra Singh Ghose on 29 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156574497/
4 this fact by producing any cogent evidence, including the call detail records of the prosecutrix and Lokendra, which could have clarified whether Lokendra had coerced her to come out or whether the victim herself had called Lokendra and asked him to take her.

sentences.text: This fact could have been proved by the prosecution by examining the call details, but unfortunately, prosecution failed to apply itself to the facts situation.

As far as, name of the father of the prosecutrix is concerned, on school admission register (Ex.P-16'C'), then we are able to read that, Kashlu has been cut and the name of PW-3 has been mentioned, which causes doubt as to the authenticity of the school admission register.

In any case, when evidence of the parents of the victim itself reveals 9 CRA-3045-2023 that, she was adult,
at the time of the incident, State having failed to prove, otherwise and justify the cutting over register (Ex.P-16'C') we are of the opinion that State has failed to make out a case for showing indulgence to enhance the sentences handed down by the learned trial Court.
20. Accordingly, CRA No. 3045 of 2022 fails and is dismissed.
21. Record of the learned trial Court be sent back.
